# `Locale`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Locale — opaque BCP-47 locale handle + locale-aware case mapping.

Default `String.toUpper`/`toLower`/`casefold` remain locale-independent —
they are correct for most scripts.  This module adds an explicit-locale
surface for the cases where language context changes the result.

The classic example: in Turkish and Azerbaijani, the lowercase dotted `i`
uppercases to capital dotted `İ` (U+0130), NOT to the ASCII `I` that the
locale-independent path produces.  Similarly, capital `I` lowercases to
dotless `ı` (U+0131).

A `Locale` is opaque and can only be constructed via `fromTag`.  An invalid
BCP-47 tag is a typed absence (`Nothing`), never a silent default.

Example:

    import Ipe.Locale as Locale

    turkishLocale : Maybe Locale
    turkishLocale = Locale.fromTag "tr"

    -- "i" → "İ"  (correct Turkish uppercase)
    example : String
    example =
        case turkishLocale of
            Just tr -> String.toUpperIn tr "i"
            Nothing -> String.toUpper "i"   -- fallback

## `Locale`

An opaque, parse-validated BCP-47 locale.

Constructed only via `fromTag`; never a bare string cast.

## `fromTag`

```ipe
fromTag : String -> Maybe Locale
```

`fromTag tag` — attempt to parse `tag` as a BCP-47 language tag.

Returns `Nothing` if the string is not a structurally valid BCP-47 tag.
An invalid tag is always a typed absence, never a silent fallback to a
default locale.

Valid examples: `"en"`, `"tr"`, `"en-US"`, `"zh-Hant-TW"`.

## `toTag`

```ipe
toTag : Locale -> String
```

`toTag locale` — recover the BCP-47 tag string from a `Locale`.
